---
title: eoread
subtitle: "Read satellite products as xarray Datasets"
---

## What is eoread?

eoread provides a modular implementation of satellite data input/output built on [xarray](https://docs.xarray.dev/) and [dask](https://docs.dask.org/). It offers unified readers for a wide range of Earth observation satellite products, returning lazy `xarray.Dataset` objects ready for subsetting, processing, and analysis.

## Features

- **Unified API** — Each (sensor, level) has a reader class (`Level1C_MSI`, `Level2_OLCI`, …) under `eoread.readers` that returns a consistent `xarray.Dataset` with canonical variable names.
- **Lazy loading** — All raster data are backed by dask arrays; nothing is computed at construction, enabling out-of-core and parallel processing.
- **Canonical schema** — Every dataset is validated against the locked output schema at read time (stamped with a `schema_version` attribute); unsupported products fail loudly.
- **Quality flags on demand** — No pre-decoded masks are stored; readers decode boolean flag layers from the raw data when asked (`getflag`).
- **Chunking control** — All readers accept a `chunks` parameter for tuning spatial block sizes to match your workload.

## Supported Sensors

| Category | Sensors |
|----------|----------|
| ESA Sentinel | Sentinel-2 MSI, Sentinel-3 OLCI, MERIS |
| Landsat | Landsat 8/9 OLI |
| NASA | MODIS, ECOSTRESS, PACE OCI, HICO |
| Other | VENµS, SGLI, HYPSO-1, PRISMA, GOES-NG, GEOSAT, Pleiades, Pleiades Neo, PlanetScope |

## Installation

```bash
hyp add --hygeos eoread
```

## Quick Example

```python
from eoread.readers.msi import Level1C_MSI

# Calling the reader class returns a lazy xarray.Dataset directly
ds = Level1C_MSI("S2B_MSIL1C_20250320T104639_N0511_R051_T31UDS_20250320T142408.SAFE",
                 chunks=1000, resolution=60)

# Inspect the dataset
print(ds)
```

## Migrating from v1

The pre-v2 readers (`eoread.legacy.*`, including the `Level1()`/`Level2()`
auto-detection functions) were removed in 2.0. Existing chains built on the v1
layout can still be served from a v2 dataset with `eoread.compat.v1`, which maps
it back to the legacy variable names and structure (a few sensors carry
documented clean breaks — see `eoread.compat.CLEAN_BREAKS`).

For more detailed examples, see the [Getting Started](articles/getting-started.qmd) guide.
